title: Grade 7 Science — Tue, May 26
description: Nutrition in Plants — Day 2 of 5: Photosynthesis in detail
subject: science

questions.question: Photosynthesis takes place in the presence of:
questions.explanation: Sunlight is essential for photosynthesis — without it, the plant cannot produce food.

questions.question: Which test is used to check if a leaf has made starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. A leaf that has done photosynthesis will show this colour change.

questions.question: To test for starch in a leaf, we first boil it in alcohol to:
questions.explanation: Boiling in alcohol removes the green chlorophyll so that iodine colour change can be clearly seen.

questions.question: A variegated leaf (partly green, partly white) shows starch ONLY in:
questions.explanation: Only green parts have chlorophyll and can do photosynthesis. White parts lack chlorophyll → no photosynthesis → no starch.

questions.question: Sunlight energy in photosynthesis is captured by:
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight energy and uses it to convert CO₂ and water into glucose.

questions.question: When is the rate of photosynthesis highest in a plant?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis rate is highest when there is maximum sunlight — usually midday on a bright day.

questions.question: The food made by plants during photosynthesis is:
options: Glucose (which converts to starch for storage)
questions.explanation: Glucose is directly made in photosynthesis. It is later converted to starch for storage in leaves.

questions.question: How does CO₂ enter the leaf?
questions.explanation: Stomata are tiny pores (mostly on the underside of leaves) through which CO₂ enters and O₂ exits.

questions.question: Guard cells control the opening and closing of:
questions.explanation: Each stomatal pore is surrounded by two guard cells that swell (open stomata) or shrink (close stomata) based on water availability.

questions.question: If a plant is kept in the dark for several days, what happens?
options: It cannot make food; leaves may turn yellow
questions.explanation: Without light, photosynthesis stops. Stored food is used up; leaves lose their green colour (etiolation).

questions.question: In an experiment, a plant is covered with a black bag. The iodine test on leaves will show:
questions.explanation: Without light, no photosynthesis occurs, so no starch is made. Iodine shows no colour change (brown remains).

questions.question: Which gas released by plants is essential for all living things to breathe?
questions.explanation: Oxygen released by plants during photosynthesis makes it breathable for animals and humans.

questions.question: Water is transported from roots to leaves through:
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels carry water and minerals from roots upward through stems to leaves.

questions.question: Why are leaves broad and flat?
options: To maximise surface area for absorbing sunlight
questions.explanation: The broad, flat shape of leaves maximises surface area to capture as much sunlight as possible for photosynthesis.

questions.question: The process by which plants make food from CO₂ and H₂O using sunlight is called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis (photo = light, synthesis = making) is the food-making process in plants.
